title: Optimize kernel-matching and prefill/decode scheduling across MIG stripes and clock regimes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce p99 decode latency and improve steady-state throughput on mixed fleets (H100, L40S, A10) by improving kernel selection heuristics and making prefill/decode scheduling MIG-aware and clock-sensitive. This ticket covers investigation, microbenchmarks, scheduler changes, and a canary rollout with observability dashboards.

Background:
- Recent capacity incidents showed large tail latency increases when low-power clock governors are applied to H100 nodes and when MIG stripes are heavily multiplexed with mixed-sequence workloads.
- We currently pick kernels primarily based on model size and quant type and use a simple prefill-vs-decode allocator that doesn't account for MIG stripe isolation or clock state.

Hypothesis:
1) For H100 and L40S, some kernels (fused attention vs windowed attention) perform better at higher clocks and on full GPU (no MIG). On tightly partitioned MIG stripes, smaller kernels with lower register pressure have less variance.
2) Prefill work (long prefix) benefits from kernels optimized for throughput; decode (short-step) benefits from low-latency kernels and aggressive KV caching. If scheduler co-locates many decode-heavy streams on the same MIG stripe, p99 suffers.

What we did:
- Built a microbenchmark harness that runs attention kernels across H100/L40S/A10 at different clock limits and MIG configurations. Harness code and results: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hw-perf-bench/tree/eng-13789.
- Collected 5000 sample runs per kernel/clock/MIG combination using representative prompt length distribution (prefill mean 1024 tokens, decode steps 1-64). Raw CSVs: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/data/hw-kernel-bench/ENG-13789.
- Implemented a lightweight kernel scoring function in runtime that consumes: model_arch, quant, seq_len_hint, current_clock_bin, and MIG_capacity_hint. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4567.

Key findings (summary numbers):
- H100 full-GPU + clocks at 1.3 GHz: fused attention kernel shows 18% lower median latency and 12% lower p99 for decode steps vs baseline.
- H100 2x1g.10 MIG stripes at same clocks: fused kernel p99 regresses by ~25% due to increased SM register pressure and context-switching; smaller tiled kernel is 10% better p99 on MIG.
- L40S shows consistent gains for the tiled kernel when sequence length < 256 regardless of clock governor, likely due to L2 bandwidth characteristics.
- A10 is more sensitive to kernel selection for FP16 vs INT8 quant paths; INT8 quantization + tiled kernel gives best cost/throughput trade-off.

Decisions taken:
- Adopt a two-stage kernel selection heuristic: preferred_kernel = score_by_hardware(clock_bin, mig_capacity) + score_by_seq_and_quant(seq_hint, model_arch). This biases toward fused kernels only when on full GPUs and high-clock bins.
- Make prefill/decode scheduler MIG-aware: enforce a soft quota so that decode-heavy low-latency lanes are spread across MIG stripes to avoid tail amplification.
- Add clock_bin telemetry to the routing table and SLIs so autoscaler and routing policies can avoid low-clock nodes for latency-sensitive tiers.

Implementation details:
- New runtime config keys: kernel_scheduler.policy ("hardware_aware_v1"), prefill_scheduler.mig_balance_threshold (float), and hardware.telemetry.clock_bin (enum). All are feature gated behind runtime-1.20 flag.
- Kernel scoring function implemented as a compact table (no heavy ML) with entries populated from bench results. The runtime falls back to previous behavior if a match isn't found.
- Prefill/Decode scheduler change: added a per-MIG stripe decode_count metric and a rebalance loop that will prioritize placing decode requests on MIG stripes with decode_count < threshold. Rebalance respects affinity and isolation constraints.

Performance validated:
- Canary (5% traffic) on dedicated-h100-prod fleet for two weeks: p50 decode latency unchanged, p95 improved by 9%, p99 improved by 13% for customer-tier latency-sensitive routes. Overall token throughput for batch workloads improved 4% on H100 full-GPU runs.
- Cost note: On mixed fleets, scheduler avoids using throttled low-clock nodes for latency-sensitive routes; this increases hourly GPU cost for those routes by ~7% but reduces error budgets and customer-visible tail latency.

Reviews and feedback:
- PM (Leah Morgan): approves the trade-off for latency-sensitive tiers but asked for a compensation plan to lower cost for best-effort tiers. Added follow-up subtask to add a cost-tiering knob.
- Design (Nikhil Rao): requested clearer Console visualization of clock_bin and per-MIG stripe decode load. Created design ticket DES-214 for dashboard mockups.
- Security (Rina Chen): scoped minimal review required; no secret material surfaced. Marked security_review_required=false.

Open issues / blockers:
- Edge case: very small models running in heavily time-multiplexed MIG stripes still show unrecoverable p99 spikes. Follow-up needed to support pin-to-full-gpu fallback for such models (possible perf/cost trade-offs).
- Some cloud providers do not expose stable clock governor telemetry; fallback heuristics required. See dependency ENG-12100 (cloud-metrics-unification).

Next steps / action items (owner):
- Miguel S: finish integration tests for kernel_scheduler.policy and add unit tests for table lookup (ETA 2026-03-18).
- Asha P: coordinate with PM to define cost-tiering knob and add to runtime config (ETA 2026-03-22).
- Infra: enable clock telemetry for a select L40S pool (dependency ENG-12850).
- Release lead: plan runtime-1.20 canary expansion to 20% after deterministic results on current canary (target 2026-03-28).

Notes from on-call incident 2026-02-10 that motivated work:
- Incident summary: p99 spikes correlated with autoscaler placing latency-tier traffic onto newly-added H100 nodes under constrained cloud clock settings. Root cause: scheduler chose fused kernel without regard for MIG partitioning or clock bin. Lessons incorporated into this ticket: add hardware binning and conservative defaults when telemetry missing.

Summary: Implemented a hardware-aware kernel picker and a MIG-aware prefill/decode scheduler, validated across H100/L40S/A10, and deployed as a canary. The changes improve p99 for latency-sensitive traffic at modest incremental cost. Remaining work: widen canary, cost-tiering config, and a fallback path for tiny models on heavily multiplexed MIG stripes.
